title: Council compensation approved for 2026–2030 term
subtitle: Also: Enova board appointment, Victoria Street traffic fixes, transit hub communications plan, Sri Lanka women's leadership delegation visit.
overview: At a special meeting, Council approved the consultant's compensation recommendations for the 2026-2030 term {{vote:m3}}. The amended motion had the mayor's pay follow the consultant's report instead of a 10.3% increase. It also funds the gap between the 50th and 60th percentile through Kitchener Utilities, citing Council's governing role over the municipally owned gas utility. Staff will update the compensation policy and review pay again before the 2030 election.

Council also appointed an independent director to the Enova Energy Corporation board {{vote:m2}}. Two motions on the Victoria Street North and Ahrens Street West area near the Kitchener GO/VIA station were approved. One directs staff to work with Regional staff on intersection changes and winter maintenance before winter 2026 {{vote:m4}}. The other calls for a communications plan and community meetings before 2027 on transit hub and GO expansion construction {{vote:m5}}.
Earlier, Council hosted a delegation from Sri Lanka taking part in a federal municipal partnership on women's leadership and inclusive services. Council then met in closed session.

decisions.detail: Council approved the consultant's compensation recommendations for the 2026-2030 term, with the mayor's pay following the report rather than a 10.3% increase, as passed {{vote:m3}}.
The difference between the 50th and 60th percentile will be funded through Kitchener Utilities, and staff will update the Council compensation policy and run another review before the 2030 election.
Cong-Rong Xie was appointed as an independent director of Enova Energy Corporation until the 2027 annual general meeting {{vote:m2}}.

decisions.item: Victoria Street North and Ahrens Street West traffic
decisions.detail: Staff will work with Regional staff to review temporary and permanent intersection changes, such as left turn restrictions and stop bar placement, and to improve winter maintenance before winter 2026 {{vote:m4}}.

decisions.item: Transit hub and GO expansion communications
decisions.detail: Staff will coordinate with the Region and Metrolinx on a communications plan and community meetings before 2027 for residents, businesses, neighbourhood associations and elected officials {{vote:m5}}.

debate: On compensation, discussion at the resumed meeting was mostly about procedure. One councillor said they wanted to change an earlier vote and asked to bring back the consultant's mayoral figure in place of the 10.3% increase. The Mayor explained that the change had to be made as an amendment to the committee motion.

Several councillors described the Victoria Street North and Ahrens Street West area as congested and hard to navigate. They cited traffic at train times and pedestrian crossings, and one tied it to the city's Vision Zero commitment.

The mover said the timing matters because Regional design work points to construction on Victoria Street in 2027. The mover also said last winter it was unclear whether the City, the Region or Metrolinx was responsible for clearing snow.

On the communications plan, the mover pointed to last spring's train horn problems, which involved several levels of government, and said nearby neighbourhoods should not be an afterthought in construction planning.
The Mayor suggested Council may later ask the Region to bring back project teams that included local councillors, a practice that had been dropped. A councillor agreed.
